P10A-H01.name: Positive Realized Spread After Maker Fees
P10A-H01.rationale: Passive limit orders placed at the inside quote earn the half-spread upon execution and incur maker fees (or rebates) rather than paying taker fee penalties. If the subsequent midpoint price movement does not fully erode the half-spread, the realized spread retained after maker fees will be strictly positive.
P10A-H01.measurable_prediction: Mean realized spread at the 1-second and 5-second post-fill markout horizons exceeds the exchange maker fee schedule (e.g., > 1.0 bps on Binance.US tier 1 maker fees) with p < 0.01.
P10A-H01.statistical_test: Stationary block-bootstrap one-sample t-test (H0: mean realized spread <= 0)
P10A-H01.economic_gate: Mean realized spread > 0.0 bps across all non-stressed validation regimes
P10A-H01.rejection_criterion: Mean realized spread <= 0.0 bps at the 5-second markout horizon, or bootstrap p >= 0.05.

P10A-H02.name: Queue Position Determinism of Realized Profitability
P10A-H02.rationale: In price-time priority matching engines, orders joined at the back of the queue (top of queue depth high) only execute when incoming taker volume is large enough to deplete earlier orders, which strongly correlates with adverse momentum and toxic flow. Orders executed near the front of the queue experience significantly lower adverse selection.
P10A-H02.measurable_prediction: Fills occurring from the front tercile of estimated queue depth display statistically significant higher net markout (at least +3.0 bps higher) than fills occurring from the back tercile (p < 0.001).
P10A-H02.metric: Queue Position Markout Delta = E[Markout | Queue_front] - E[Markout | Queue_back]
P10A-H02.statistical_test: Two-sample Mann-Whitney U test and Welch t-test on front vs back queue tercile markouts
P10A-H02.economic_gate: Markout difference between front and back queue terciles >= 2.0 bps
P10A-H02.rejection_criterion: Queue position markout delta < 1.0 bps or failure to reject null at alpha = 0.01.

P10A-H03.name: Adverse Selection Offsetting Quoted Spread
P10A-H03.rationale: Taker orders arriving at the book carry informed flow. Fills on passive limit orders suffer from immediate price drift in the direction of the aggressive order (adverse selection), eroding a substantial fraction of the quoted half-spread.
P10A-H03.measurable_prediction: The adverse price movement (markout drift) within 5 seconds of execution offsets at least 60% of the initial half-spread across liquid spot crypto pairs.
P10A-H03.metric: Adverse Selection Ratio = E[Adverse Price Drift (5s)] / E[Quoted Half-Spread]
P10A-H03.statistical_test: Block bootstrap confidence interval on the adverse selection ratio (H0: ratio < 0.50)
P10A-H03.economic_gate: Quantification of adverse selection ratio with lower 95% bootstrap bound > 0.50
P10A-H03.rejection_criterion: Mean adverse selection ratio < 0.40 or post-fill drift is indistinguishable from zero (p >= 0.05).

P10A-H04.name: Microstructure Conditioning for Superior Fill Economics
P10A-H04.rationale: Conditioning passive order placement and cancellation on microstructure signals (order-book imbalance, recent trade flow aggression, and spread volatility) can selectively avoid toxic adverse selection fills and concentrate fills in balanced, mean-reverting regimes.
P10A-H04.measurable_prediction: Microstructure-conditioned quoting yields a net realized spread improvement of at least +2.5 bps over an unconditioned static inside quoting baseline on out-of-sample validation data (p < 0.01).
P10A-H04.metric: Conditioned Alpha Delta = Net Expectancy (Conditioned) - Net Expectancy (Static Inside)
P10A-H04.statistical_test: Paired block bootstrap difference test with Holm-Bonferroni correction
P10A-H04.economic_gate: Net expectancy improvement >= 2.0 bps with positive OOS Sharpe ratio
P10A-H04.rejection_criterion: Incremental net expectancy < 1.0 bps or paired test p-value >= 0.05.

P10A-H05.name: Inventory-Aware Quoting and Liquidation Cost Reduction
P10A-H05.rationale: Accumulating directional inventory imposes adverse price drift risk and forced aggressive liquidation costs. Skewing quotes (asymmetrically widening quotes on the side of accumulated inventory and tightening on the reducing side) reduces inventory variance and avoids costly taker liquidation.
P10A-H05.measurable_prediction: Inventory-aware quoting (Avellaneda-Stoikov style skew) reduces round-trip liquidation and inventory carrying drag by at least 40% compared to symmetric quoting, resulting in higher net expectancy.
P10A-H05.metric: Inventory Drag Ratio = Total Terminal Liquidation & Holding Drag / Cumulative Gross Spread
P10A-H05.statistical_test: Paired bootstrap test on terminal net P&L and inventory variance
P10A-H05.economic_gate: Reduction of inventory standard deviation by >= 30% without negative net expectancy impact
P10A-H05.rejection_criterion: Inventory variance reduction < 15% or net expectancy deterioration of > 1.5 bps.

P10A-H06.name: Positive Net Expectancy Under Conservative Fill and Latency Models
P10A-H06.rationale: A realistic, conservative passive market making model incorporating queue priority, cancellation latency, partial fills, and conservative maker fees can achieve positive net expectancy per round trip without assuming perfect fill rates or zero-latency cancellations.
P10A-H06.measurable_prediction: Simulated passive execution with >= 50 ms cancel latency and queue-depletion fill modeling achieves OOS net expectancy > 0.0 bps per filled round trip (p < 0.01) across BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, and SOLUSDT.
P10A-H06.metric: Net Expectancy per Round Trip (bps) after all maker fees, taker liquidation, and adverse selection
P10A-H06.statistical_test: Block bootstrap t-test against null hypothesis of non-positive net expectancy (H0: Net <= 0)
P10A-H06.economic_gate: Net expectancy > 0.0 bps per round trip in out-of-sample validation
P10A-H06.rejection_criterion: OOS net expectancy <= 0.0 bps or lower 95% bootstrap confidence bound < 0.0 bps.

P10A-H07.name: Passive Edge Robustness Under Stressed Execution Assumptions
P10A-H07.rationale: A genuine passive execution edge must remain robust to parameter degradation (increased latency, degraded fill probability, widened adverse selection, and fee increases) rather than collapsing under friction.
P10A-H07.measurable_prediction: Subjecting the model to the Phase 10A stress matrix (-10% fill probability, +25% latency, +25% slippage/adverse drift) preserves positive net expectancy (> 0.0 bps).
P10A-H07.metric: Stressed Net Expectancy (bps) across the 7-dimensional stress test matrix
P10A-H07.statistical_test: Worst-case stress scenario evaluation across block bootstrap realizations
P10A-H07.rejection_criterion: Net expectancy becomes negative (< 0.0 bps) under any single baseline stress perturbation.
